events.title: Christopher Wren is born
events.description: The future architect was born in Wiltshire, England. He went on to design 52 London churches after the Great Fire of 1666, including St Paul's Cathedral.
events.significance: Wren's work shaped the skyline of London and left a lasting mark on English architecture.

events.title: The Long March ends
events.description: The Long March, the epic retreat of China's Communist forces, came to its close. The marchers had crossed thousands of miles of difficult terrain.
events.significance: The march became a founding legend of the Chinese Communist movement and helped bring Mao Zedong to leadership.

events.title: Herbert Hoover dies
events.description: The 31st President of the United States died at the age of 90. He was an engineer and humanitarian whose single term as president coincided with the start of the Great Depression.
events.significance: Hoover's long public life ranged from large-scale famine relief to his work on government reorganization after he left office.

events.title: Sydney Opera House opens
events.description: Queen Elizabeth II officially opened Jørn Utzon's sail-roofed performing arts centre on Bennelong Point after 14 years of construction.
events.significance: The building became one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

events.title: Muammar Gaddafi is killed
events.description: Rebel forces captured Libya's longtime ruler in his hometown of Sirte, and he was killed shortly afterward.
events.significance: His death effectively ended the first Libyan civil war and the four-decade rule he had held.
